summary: auth login --chrome must query every Chrome host_key that actually holds a required cookie, not just the bare configured domain -- some tenants scope required cookies host-only to a subdomain that a same-apex query cannot see.
reason: Concur scopes the _csrf cookie host-only to the tenant's regional web subdomain (observed: us2.concursolutions.com), not the bare apex (concursolutions.com), while JWT is domain-scoped (.concursolutions.com) and visible from the apex. Real cookie-jar semantics mean a request/query against the apex never receives a host-only subdomain cookie. The profile-discovery step's SQL used a loose `host_key LIKE '%domain%'` substring match and correctly found _csrf, but the actual pycookiecheat extraction step queried only the bare apex and silently excluded it -- producing a false 'not logged in' error for a user who was, in fact, logged in with the cookie present in Chrome. This is a Printing-Press-level auth-extraction gap (any spec with a subdomain-scoped required cookie hits it), not a Concur-specific one, but is patched here first per this repo's local-patch-first convention.

changes.description: Added cookieQueryHosts() + discoverCookieHosts() to find every Chrome host_key holding a required cookie (via the same copy-then-sqlite3-query approach as inspectCookiesForDomain). extractViaPycookiecheat and extractViaPycookiecheatCLI now query every discovered host and merge results, instead of querying only the bare configured domain. extractViaCookiesCLI and extractViaCookieScoop were NOT patched (same latent bug) -- neither tool is installed in this environment and the fix could not be tested against them; tracked as a follow-up.

validated_outcome: Before: `auth login --chrome` failed with `cookie "_csrf" not found for concursolutions.com` despite an active, logged-in Chrome session. After: both required cookies found (`OK Found 2 cookies for concursolutions.com`), and a live `account whoami` call against the documented REST API returned HTTP 200 with a full SCIM user profile -- the first empirical confirmation that cookie-session auth reaches the documented v3/v4 REST host family (open question from the run's own discovery report).
